definitions.count_relationship: Normalized quotes are necessary but not sufficient for a strict original-time comparison. A zero strict count does not imply a zero normalized count.
definitions.normalized_snapshot: A quote exists in odds_snapshots and is linked to a raw provider observation. It may still be late.
definitions.strict_original_time_comparison: The quote's provider/observed and ingest times are both at or before the original prediction issue time, the provider identity is independently mapped, and the tournament edition window and participant orientation are verified.

limitations: No provider request, purchase or quota consumption.
The census describes the current production database, not an earlier snapshot of it.
A normalized quote is not proof of original-time availability.
Provider startTime and canonical start can differ; the normalizer uses the canonical start.

no_snapshot_payloads.note: Failures are failed ingest runs, not a missing market 121. The unlicensed-book bucket overlaps the time buckets and is not additive. Of the 99, 74 were post-provider-start and 25 were pre-start by provider but rejected because the canonical start had passed.

normalization_lineage.attribution_finding: odds_snapshots has no provider_code column and its source_snapshot_id uses a generic SE_LIVE_ODDS_SNAPSHOT_V1 prefix. Filtering it for an ODDSPAPI prefix returns zero even though the raw-observation lineage contains the OddsPapi quotes. Provider attribution must join raw_odds_observation_id.

original_time_timing.strict_reason: An identity before issue is only a candidate. Strict evidence also needs an independent OddsPapi tournament mapping and a verified edition window. The prior census measured 0 independent mappings, so the strict count remains zero even though a few identities arrived before issue.

payload_catalogue.finding: Actual sportId=12 tennis payloads use market 121 and outcomes 121/122. Market 171 is absent from every stored tennis payload and is Counter-Strike moneyline in the published catalogue. The 171 tutorial assumption is therefore not the root cause here.
